doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Major versus minor harmony and late Coltrane
summary: Rowe and Tolliver compare chord-colour experiences; Tolliver notes Coltrane's late work in a major feeling.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: That’s always the hardest part for me is the chord changes, finding something that’s interesting but — you had said, I really got a kick out of your story about learning about the minor nine chord in college, because I had the same experience except it was with the major seven. And for a while it was all about major sevenths. And eventually it got a little bit too happy for me so I had to —

Well you know sometimes it’s a lot more difficult to get some sort of solo activity out of major rather than minor. And as you probably know, I mean John Coltrane, he experimented with not playing in the minor you know, towards the end of his life you know. He did a lot of things off of a major feeling as opposed to a minor feeling.
